author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This parser reads Kubernetes audit events from AKS, EKS and a self-managed API server. AKS records arrive through an Azure Event Hubs integration, EKS events through S3 Ingest, and a self-managed API server's audit log file works too. Every event goes to CloudAudit.
notes:
Setup:
- AKS: stream the cluster's kube-audit (every request, high volume) or kube-audit-admin (no get or list) diagnostic category to an event hub and read it with a Sophos NG-SIEM Azure Event Hubs integration; each line is one diagnostic record with the audit event as text in properties.log.
- EKS: turn on the audit control plane log, send the cluster's log group through a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to Firehose with decompression and message extraction on, then to S3, so each line is one audit event, and read the bucket with S3 Ingest (the Sophos Fusion CloudWatch Logs page describes this path).
- A self-managed API server's audit log file works too, with or without a syslog header.

Field mapping:
- Every event goes to CloudAudit: the verb as event_name, the resource and subresource (pods/exec) as event_type, the API group as event_source (core for the core group), the user, user type and impersonated user, the first source IP, the user agent, and the response code, reason and message.
- get, list and watch are read_only.
- The request URI, namespace, name and API version go to request_parameters; the audit level, stage, groups, the authorization decision and reason, the EKS IAM ARN and the AKS category go to additional_event_data.

Made up in the samples:
- The samples leave out the apiVersion and annotations keys because the repo's sample scan reads Kubernetes API group names as hostnames.
- Samples follow the audit Event reference with made-up values.

Testing:
- Passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (117 of 117 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs, and 29 of 29 on two extra lines with the authorization annotations).
- The tenant's built-in Azure Monitor parser claims AKS records when nothing else does and leaves them generic; with this parser in place it took the AKS lines in 11 of 11 Run Tests.
- No built-in parser claimed the EKS or self-managed lines.

Known gaps:
- Other AKS categories aren't claimed.
